checks.source_quote: When solving complex spatial reasoning tasks, ordinary humans naturally revisit the scenes from task-relevant viewpoints and mentally reconstruct the spatial layouts from those viewpoints. But can Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) proactively think in the same way? We term this ability Active Spatial Mentalization (ASM), an intrinsic component of visual intelligence that remains substantially underdeveloped in current LVLMs. To bridge this gap, we introduce SpatialASM, a scalable framework to internalize ASM into LVLMs through training-time spatial simulation. SpatialASM employs an allocentric novel-view generator to ground hypothetical viewpoints in visual evidence and produces two complementary forms of supervision: i) explicit ASM trajectories that teach LVLMs when and how to adaptively invoke view planning and imagination during spatial reasoning, and ii) automatically-constructed perspective-taking tasks that further strengthen viewpoint-conditioned scene imagination. checks.source_quote: Spatial reasoning is a foundational capability for Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs), underpinning applications from autonomous driving and embodied navigation to robotic manipulation [11, 15, 37]. While LVLMs achieve strong performance on many visual tasks [2, 43, 70], they still fail on complex spatial problems that involve viewpoint transformation, cross-view correspondence, and reasoning about unobserved regions [25, 68, 69, 72]. These tasks go beyond passively extracting relations from the given observations, as they require the model to reason about the three-dimensional scene from perspectives that the input images do not directly provide.

checks.source_quote: An alternative is to attach an external world model or spatial tool at inference time to generate supplementary observations [10, 73, 80] (Fig. 2(b)). While this provides useful visual evidence, it ties spatial reasoning to an external simulator at inference time, even when the LVLM learns when to invoke it [74, 84]. Tool distillation [38, 83] removes this dependence, but targets perceptual tools such as depth and cognitive maps rather than viewpoint planning and view imagination. Most such methods also adopt an egocentric interface that reaches a target viewpoint through a sequence of camera-centric actions, so each query requires a multi-step rollout [10, 73]. Closer to our setting, World2VLM [78] uses a world model at training time, but it supervises egocentric view association without producing any reasoning trajectory.

checks.source_quote: We introduce SpatialASM, a framework that equips LVLMs with ASM capabilities by using an allocentric novel-view generator (NVG) as a training-time spatial simulation engine rather than an inference-time tool (Fig. 2(c)). Given a spatial QA sample, the NVG renders views from question-conditioned viewpoints planned by the LVLM, grounding hypothetical perspectives in concrete visual evidence. SpatialASM transforms these into two complementary forms of supervision: explicit ASM reasoning trajectories for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and automatically verifiable perspective-taking tasks for reinforcement learning with GRPO [53]. The rendered views serve only as temporary scafolding: in the final SFT data, they are replaced by text captions that describe the imagined observations, so the LVLM learns to construct spatial layouts internally from the original input images alone (Fig. 1(a)).

checks.source_quote: The design of SpatialASM is guided by two key mechanisms (Fig. 3). checks.source_quote: Our contributions are threefold. 1) We formulate Active Spatial Mentalization as the joint capability of proactively planning task-relevant viewpoints and imagining corresponding observations, and argue that the absence of ASM is a key bottleneck of spatial reasoning in current LVLMs. 2) We introduce SpatialASM, a scalable framework built on an allocentric novel-view generator and GeoP-based filtering that converts existing spatial QA data into explicit ASM trajectories for SFT and perspective-taking tasks for RL. 3) SpatialASM improves average spatial accuracy on four LVLM backbones over seven benchmarks while keeping general-VQA performance within 0.6 points.

checks.source_quote: Spatial data synthesis. Many studies enhance spatial reasoning by synthesizing large-scale datasets (Fig. 2(a)). Early approaches build on public scene datasets (e.g., ScanNet [18], ARKitScenes [4]) with 3D annotations [37, 47], or employ expert models (e.g., segmentation, depth estimation) for data curation [11, 15, 20]. Recent data engines scale further: HoliSpatial [26] renders scenes through 3D Gaussian Splatting, and VST [71] uses simulators to generate novel observations. Despite their efectiveness, the dominant supervision remains answer-only, providing the final answer but little guidance on how to actively acquire or mentally construct missing evidence. VST-R [71] takes a step towards reasoning supervision with explicit step-by-step traces, but its trajectories teach the model to derive spatial conclusions from provided evidence rather than to plan informative viewpoints and imagine unobserved perspectives. checks.source_quote: Interestingly, SpatialASM-NVG does not achieve the best GeoP as SVC obtains lower GeoP values for both LVLMs, but it consistently yields substantially higher reasoning accuracy. This observation suggests that geometric consistency alone does not fully determine the utility of generated views for downstream spatial reasoning. We attribute this to our allocentric form of viewpoint representation. Rather than describing the target viewpoint through a sequence of quantified egocentric motions, LVLMs can designate the viewpoint through a single query, and the corresponding location of the viewpoint is explicitly marked in the original input image. Therefore, our allocentric-view generation provides not only reliable novel views, but also auxiliary evidence that is more directly aligned with the reasoning objective.

checks.source_quote: In this work, we identify Active Spatial Mentalization (ASM) as a key bottleneck in LVLM spatial reasoning. To address this issue, we propose SpatialASM, a novel post-training framework that internalizes ASM capabilities into LVLMs through training-time spatial simulation. Experiments across seven spatial reasoning benchmarks and four model architectures demonstrate that SpatialASM consistently improves spatial reasoning while preserving general visual capabilities. More importantly, our framework provides a scalable approach to constructing CoT supervision for existing spatial datasets, addressing the common lack of intermediate reasoning processes in open-source spatial data. In future work, we plan to internalize other forms of tool-assisted reasoning and extend ASM to dynamic real-world scenes, embodied interaction, and longer-horizon 3D reasoning.

checks.source_quote: The recent ESI-Bench [29] delves deeper into the perception-action loop and treat it as a higher level of spatial intelligence. An agent can selectively employ locomotion, and manipulation to uncover information that cannot be resolved from the initial observation alone. By reasoning under the active multiple setting, where the models can proactively execute movements and interact with the simulation environments, the performance significantly outperforms that under the passive single setting. However, the accuracy of the active multiple setting lags far behind the GT passive setting, where the best ground-truth passive trajectories are provided. These results suggest that current LVLMs lack intrinsic proactive exploration capability when solving spatial problems, unless they are explicitly prompted to do so. And their trajectory-planning capability is still far from saturated.

checks.assessment: 核对三点：(1) GeoThinker 及 geometry-enhanced 方法 [36,81] 确实引入额外预训练特征分支与架构特定融合模块、需几何-语义表示对齐，批注转述无误；(2) “our ASM operates at the viewpoint and observation level”与“不同于其 feature-retrieval 层面的主动”对应“上升层面”的表述；(3) “data-centric pipeline...of-the-shelf post-training strategies without introducing geometry module or making architectural modification”支持“无需额外分支或架构改动”。原文未在本节展开 ASM 全称与具体实现，批注未添补，未超出证据；逐字保留。
checks.source_quote: To internalize the thinking pattern of ‘perception-active loop’ into LVLMs, Geothinker [36] proposes active geometry integration, in which semantic representations selectively query task-relevant geometric features. However, such geometry-enhanced approaches [36, 81] introduce an additional pretrained feature branch and architecture-specific fusion modules into the LVLMs, and require alignment between geometric and semantic representations, potentially limiting their adaptability across heterogeneous VLM architectures. Unlike their notion of ‘active’ at the feature-retrieval level, our ASM operates at the viewpoint and observation level. It reasons about where useful evidence should be acquired and what should be observed from the corresponding hypothetical viewpoint. And we focus on data-centric pipeline where such capability can be internalized through of-the-shelf post-training strategies without introducing geometry module or making architectural modification.

checks.source_quote: A wide spectrum of previous work lay emphasis on large-scale high-quality data curation pipeline to improve spatial reasoning in LVLMs. A straightforward approach is to construct such supervision via human annotation [8], but it is hardly afordable to scale. Some other pipelines resort to proprietary/open-source large-language models [15, 52]. However, current models’ performance on relatively challenging spatial reasoning tasks, especially in multi-view or video modalities, remains far from satisfactory and may introduce abundant errors to curated QA pairs.

checks.assessment: 核对数字与条件：VST-R 为 135K 条带显式逐步推理轨迹的样本；合成需场景中的 ground-truth 3D bounding boxes 生成中间 BEV 图像；监督教模型从给定视觉证据推结论，而非感知—行动闭环；尚未公开发布。SpatialASM 无需前置 GT 3D 标注，建模“何时需要额外视角、应在何处心理观察、预期何种证据”。初稿准确，仅补充 135K 与 GT 3D 框用途等细节，无超出原文的因果。
checks.source_quote: VST-R [71] constitutes an important step towards reasoning supervision by providing 135K curated sample with explicit step-by-step reasoning traces. However, its synthesis process requires ground-truth 3D bounding boxes in the original scene data to form intermediate Bird’s-Eye View (BEV) images. Moreover, its reasoning supervision primarily teaches the model to derive spatial conclusions from the provided visual evidence, rather than to execute the perception-action loop of proactive exploration. It is not yet publicly released as well. In contrast, SpatialASM grounds an explicit question-conditioned reasoning process of when additional viewpoint reasoning is needed, where the model should mentally observe, and what evidence should be expected from that viewpoint, which is more demanding and human-like. Importantly, SpatialASM can synthesize ASM reasoning trajectories for existing spatial QA data without requiring any prerequisite ground-truth 3D annotations.

checks.source_quote: World2VLM [78] is particularly relevant to our work in that it also employs a generative world model in its data engine and distills its spatial imagination into the LVLMs. World2VLM synthesizes future views based on given parameterized camera trajectories to teach LVLMs to associate multi-view observations with egocentric motion transitions. checks.source_quote: In Sec. 3.3 we introduce the answer selection strategy to reduce potential ambiguity in the two multi-choice tasks and ensure the quality of the rendered images. A pre-defined parameter $\theta _ { R L }$ is applied in this strategy. During the construction process, we find that generated images generally have higher GeoP values when the queried allocentric viewpoint is set to backwards than when it is set to other directions. This is because the backward direction is more likely to reveal regions not visible in the input images, requiring the NVG to synthesize more unobserved content. Therefore, even when the generated images exhibit similar levels of geometric consistency, those generated for the backward direction tend to receive higher GeoP. After manually inspecting a large number of generated images and their corresponding GeoP values, we set to $\theta _ { R L }$ to 1.2 for images whose corresponding target direction is backwards, and 0.6 for all other directions.

checks.source_quote: We introduce SpatialASM, a framework that equips LVLMs with ASM capabilities by using an allocentric novel-view generator (NVG) as a training-time spatial simulation engine rather than an inference-time tool (Fig. 2(c)). Given a spatial QA sample, the NVG renders views from question-conditioned viewpoints planned by the LVLM, grounding hypothetical perspectives in concrete visual evidence. SpatialASM transforms these into two complementary forms of supervision: explicit ASM reasoning trajectories for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and automatically verifiable perspective-taking tasks for reinforcement learning with GRPO [53]. The rendered views serve only as temporary scafolding: in the final SFT data, they are replaced by text captions that describe the imagined observations, so the LVLM learns to construct spatial layouts internally from the original input images alone (Fig. 1(a)).

checks.source_quote: In this work, we identify Active Spatial Mentalization (ASM) as a key bottleneck in LVLM spatial reasoning. To address this issue, we propose SpatialASM, a novel post-training framework that internalizes ASM capabilities into LVLMs through training-time spatial simulation. Experiments across seven spatial reasoning benchmarks and four model architectures demonstrate that SpatialASM consistently improves spatial reasoning while preserving general visual capabilities. More importantly, our framework provides a scalable approach to constructing CoT supervision for existing spatial datasets, addressing the common lack of intermediate reasoning processes in open-source spatial data. In future work, we plan to internalize other forms of tool-assisted reasoning and extend ASM to dynamic real-world scenes, embodied interaction, and longer-horizon 3D reasoning.

checks.source_quote: Our contributions are threefold. 1) We formulate Active Spatial Mentalization as the joint capability of proactively planning task-relevant viewpoints and imagining corresponding observations, and argue that the absence of ASM is a key bottleneck of spatial reasoning in current LVLMs. 2) We introduce SpatialASM, a scalable framework built on an allocentric novel-view generator and GeoP-based filtering that converts existing spatial QA data into explicit ASM trajectories for SFT and perspective-taking tasks for RL. 3) SpatialASM improves average spatial accuracy on four LVLM backbones over seven benchmarks while keeping general-VQA performance within 0.6 points.
